about: LEDGER 1756 S5, ADR-0982, ADR-0635. The yadgarhq/actions hook block each consumer class carries, as data.
A consumer's class is its ONE `yadgar-class-<name>` topic. `scripts/fan_out.py` renders a consumer's yadgarhq/actions block from this file and a tag.

MEASURED, NOT CHOSEN: every list below is the hook set the class's consumers carried on 2026-10-21 (fixtures in scripts/tests/fixtures/fan_out/, each with its source commit in test_fan_out.py). S4 records what exists; this file does not decide which hooks a class should carry.

ORDER is part of the class. Where consumers of one class disagreed on order, the majority wins; on a tie, the order the other rust classes share wins. Each class's `order` field says which repositories that moves.

`live` ARMS A TAG PUSH (first-run safety, review of actions#124). While it is false, a pushed tag runs the fan-out DRY; a dispatch from main with dry_run=false is the explicit human path. Set it true only in a reviewed pull request, after a dry run from main; that pull request's own tag is then the first live run.
Keys on a hook other than `id` are written into the consumer's block as they are (only `exclude` is measured today). `overrides` replaces a hook's keys for one repository.

`sweep` is YAADGAAR 442 (c): `scripts/sweep.py` merges an adoption pull request only when every condition in its docstring holds. `sweep.live` ARMS IT and is true now; it was set in a reviewed pull request after dry runs from main. Set it false to disarm. `sweep.soak_hours` is 0.5 (ADR-1068, Max 2026-10-29): a tag younger than that is not adopted. `sweep.exclude` names a consumer the sweeper never touches, and why.

`private_consumers` is YAADGAAR 231, ADR-0983 step 2. `scripts/hook_tools_adopted.py` refuses a pull request that moves a hook-asserted tool's `version` while a consumer's rev does not accept the new version. It reads public consumers with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which cannot see a private one, so each private consumer carries ONE reviewed entry here: `{"rev": "vX.Y.Z"}`, the rev it pins, judged like a public rev; or `{"exempt": "why"}`, ADR-0983's explicit exemption. A rev, never a flag: an old rev computes as behind, so the entry cannot go stale silently. Update the rev in the pull request that moves a tool. Every `sweep.exclude` name the public listing cannot see needs an entry. Revs read 2026-10-30 from each repository's main.

`rust_bump` is ADR-1120: `.github/workflows/rust-bump.yaml` opens one bot pull request per public Rust repository whose Rust version fields differ from `versions.yaml` rust-toolchain (`scripts/rust_propagate.py`). `rust_bump.live` ARMS ITS SCHEDULE AND PUSH TRIGGER and is true now (armed in yadgarhq/actions#165, rollout step 3). Set it false to disarm.

exclude.docs: Private: the public-only listing never reaches it, and R1 would refuse it. The report renders this entry from here, so it says why it is never swept.
exclude.argocd-verify: Private: the public-only listing never reaches it, and R1 would refuse it. The report renders this entry from here, so it says why it is never swept.

exempt.actions: The producer. Its own .pre-commit-config.yaml runs its hooks from local paths (`repo: local`) at the commit under test, so it pins no rev to adopt.
exempt..github: The organisation default community-health repository (the pull request template, yaadgaar 316). Not a consumer: it carries no class topic and pins no rev to adopt.

chart.order: config and platform (2) put actionlint before helm-lint; chart (1) has the reverse. Majority: chart moves.

rust-lib.order: store and telemetry disagree on where no-compiled-in-defaults goes, one each. Tie: the place rust-app, rust-helm and service share (after observe-coverage, before run-block-size). Both move.

service.order: gateway, iam, project, task and task-db (5) put the complexity pair after cargo-clippy; iam-db and project-db (2) put it after boot-reads-watched. Majority: iam-db and project-db move.
